name: HC-SR505 mini PIR motion sensor
description: Miniature passive-infrared motion sensor module: OUT goes high (about 3.3 V from the on-board regulator) when a warm body moves within about 3 m in a cone under 100 degrees, and stays high for about 8 s (+/-30 %), re-triggering while motion continues. Sensitivity and hold time are fixed. Draws under 60 uA and runs from 4.5-20 V. Sold as: HC-SR505 mini PIR motion sensor module (10 x 23 mm green board with 10 mm white dome lens, 3-pin header +, OUT (S), -).
eli5: A tiny heat-motion detector: when a person or animal moves in front of it, it sets its output pin high for about 8 seconds.

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Motion output (marked S or OUT): about 3.3 V for ~8 s per trigger, 0 V otherwise. Safe for 3.3 V GPIOs (middle pin 2).

supplierQuery: HC-SR505 mini PIR motion sensor module
buildNotes: Header order: + (VCC), S/OUT, - (GND). OUT is always the middle pin; check the + mark before powering.
Power it from 5V (VBUS/VIN), not 3V3: the module needs 4.5-20 V. OUT stays at about 3.3 V, so it connects straight to a GPIO.
OUT is active high: 1 for about 8 s after motion (re-triggered while motion continues), then 0. The hold time and sensitivity cannot be adjusted.
Give it up to a minute after power-up to settle before trusting the output.
Point the dome where people move across its view; it senses moving warm bodies, not still ones, and cannot see through glass.

driver.code:
# HC-SR505 mini PIR motion sensor module, MicroPython driver.
# The module has the PIR element, its detector IC and a 3.3 V regulator on board.
# OUT is a push-pull logic output from the 3.3 V rail:
#   HIGH (about 3.3 V) while motion is detected; it stays high for the hold time
#   (default 8 s +/- 30 %) and re-triggers while motion continues (repeatable trigger).
#   LOW (0 V) otherwise.
# Because OUT comes from the on-board 3.3 V regulator it connects straight to a
# 3.3 V GPIO even when the module is powered from 5 V. No pull-up/down is needed.
# Supply 4.5-20 V on "+": it will not work reliably from 3.3 V.
from machine import Pin


class HCSR505:
    def __init__(self, out_pin):
        self.pin = Pin(out_pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(out_pin, int) else out_pin

    def motion(self):
        """True while the sensor reports motion (OUT high)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 1

    def on_change(self, handler):
        """Call handler(motion: bool) on every edge of OUT. Pass None to stop."""
        if handler is None:
            self.pin.irq(handler=None)
            return
        self.pin.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING | Pin.IRQ_FALLING,
                     handler=lambda p: handler(p.value() == 1))

example.code:
from hc_sr505 import HCSR505
import time

pir = HCSR505({OUT})
while True:
    print('MOTION=%d' % pir.motion())
    time.sleep(0.5)
